policy_validity.effective_date_basis: The official pages did not state a policy start date; this snapshot is supported only from the observed-active date and must not be back-cast.

acceptance_objective.rule: A Research Article must satisfy PLOS ONE's seven scientific, ethical, reporting, data, originality, and intelligibility criteria; perceived importance is not the publication threshold.

scientific_gates.rule: The study presents original research of an eligible article type.
Reported results have not already been published in the peer-reviewed literature or submitted in parallel, subject to stated preprint and related-work rules.
Experiments, statistics, and analyses meet a high technical standard and are described in sufficient detail.
Conclusions are appropriately stated and supported by the data.
The article is intelligible, clear, correct, and unambiguous in standard English.
The research meets applicable experimentation ethics and research-integrity standards.
The article follows appropriate reporting guidelines and community data-availability standards.

novelty_gate.rule: Eligible original research and honest positioning are required, but novelty of a method or state-of-the-art performance is not a separate importance-style gate; replication work can be eligible with scientific rationale.

impact_gate.rule: Peer review determines technical rigor and scientific/ethical eligibility rather than whether the paper reaches a perceived importance threshold.

breadth_gate.rule: Broad or interdisciplinary significance is not one of the seven Research Article publication criteria.

audience_interest_gate.rule: The exact criteria do not impose a separate audience-interest threshold beyond scope, intelligibility, and contribution to the scholarly record.

burden_of_doubt.rule: No reviewed exact rule creates a favorable presumption for an uncertain scientific, ethical, reporting, or data criterion; equally, reviewers must not invent an impact threshold.

allowed_repair_routes.constraint: Additional evidence is required only where data and analyses do not support the claims or technical rigor remains inadequate.
Authors should avoid overstating conclusions and may identify implications as hypotheses rather than conclusions when the data do not establish them.
The revised article must actually satisfy applicable reporting and data standards.
Original reviewers are often asked to evaluate revisions and responses; editor closure remains controlling.

review_model.triage: Editors select reviewers with relevant expertise and assess eligibility under PLOS ONE criteria and policy.
review_model.reviewers: Reviewers assess validity and quality using a structured form; identity is hidden by default unless the reviewer signs.
review_model.vote_rule: The editor makes the final decision from reviews, criteria, and independent assessment; decisions are not necessarily majority rule.
review_model.revision_model: Original reviewers may re-review revised manuscripts, while editors can identify optional or policy-misaligned reviewer requests.

ai_confidentiality_policy.author_ai_use: AI contributions must be reported in Methods or Acknowledgements with tools, uses, validation, and affected content; authors remain responsible for accuracy, attribution, citations, and their own scientific ideas.
ai_confidentiality_policy.reviewer_ai_use: AI cannot serve as a reviewer or decision editor; any use must be disclosed, and submission content must not be uploaded to generative-AI or other external services.
ai_confidentiality_policy.confidentiality: Unpublished submissions and peer-review correspondence are strictly confidential unless an explicit sharing option applies; editors and reviewers must not upload submission content to generative-AI platforms.

certification_layer.notes: No article-level certification scheme separate from PLOS ONE acceptance was identified in the reviewed exact sources. Homepage highlighting is explicitly not part of editorial decision making.
